reachable: Yes — and the mechanism is training-only by construction, which is the correct place for it. The objective is loaded at eval/adapter.py:115 and used only inside evolve/harness.py:_train (line 100/102); grep finds no reference to load_objective or a loss_fn anywhere in evolve/cups_probe.py, evolve/cups_ca.py or the scoring path. It therefore does not run at the scored read position at all; it reaches the scored position only through learned weights, exactly as the hypothesis states. It also has no branch on observation presence, so the "switches itself off exactly where it is judged" hazard does not apply. Gradient in training is real and was executed: both mechanisms differentiate through pred (dist2 via pw = pred*sqrt_w; align = (err*tgt).sum - err@tgt.T), and dim_w is deliberately detached under no_grad since it is a target-geometry quantity. A 12-step run of the real H._train with the full genome (r18 arch + r18 optim + r6 batcher + r4 stream + r2 head) on synthetic sequences returned ok=True with finite gradients. Degenerate batches are handled: all-identical targets -> `usable` False -> falls back to per-row MSE; n=1 -> MSE; empty-ring rows are gated to exactly 0 with no NaN. The two mechanisms also each carry weight — ablating them on a content-swap probe gives gap +0.319 (neither), +0.363 (hinge only), +0.553 (metric only), +0.598 (full), so mechanism (1) is the dominant contributor, matching the hypothesis's own ranking.
solves_outside_model: Clean. The objective's signature is loss(pred, tgt) with WANTS_CTX deliberately unset, so the harness calls it without ctx (harness.py:102). The impl contains no string handling of any kind — no command text, no path parsing, no move-chain resolution, nothing written into the model's input. Everything it computes is a function of the two tensors it is handed plus the batch's own target-target geometry, and all of it is discarded after training. The claim on hypothesis.txt lines 100-106 is accurate. The one place in this genome where commands ARE parsed is the inherited r4 stream, which encodes each command's OWN literal path arguments per command string in isolation (cache keyed on the command string; no cross-step state), so it carries no resolved routing — and that axis is the one the read-token-parity invariant covers, which is already established as passing.
summary: The code does what the hypothesis says, and the central claim survives the strongest test I could run. Every algebraic assertion is exact under execution: the decision identity ||p-t_j||^2-||p-t_i||^2 = ||t_i-t_j||^2 + 2e_i.(t_i-t_j) holds to 2e-7; the code's `arg` equals (0.5 - slack)/0.2 with slack the raw gap-normalised decision quantity to 1.4e-6; the matmul form of v_d equals the direct ring-weighted double sum to 1.9e-6 on a scale of 10; per-pair unit directions sum to 1. The stated data fact is real, not asserted: in evolve/jail_data/train_sample.jsonl, mv (172), `cat >` (30) and `cat >>` (51) of 724 steps all carry exit 0 with empty output, and realenv/seq_worldmodel.py:38 renders every one of them to the identical string "cwd=/ exit=0\n" — 35% of command rows are one bit-identical target block, so the equivalence quotient is motivated by the data rather than by analogy. The eval's decision variable really is unweighted mean squared-L2 (evolve/cups_probe.py:_nway line 146 and the donor bank at line 418), so the hinge is genuinely expressed in the metric the eval ranks in. The behavioural claims hold too: dim_w collapses to ~1 (std 0.05) under isotropic target differences, and concentrates (1.79 vs 0.98) on the coordinates that separate confusable targets when those differences live in a coordinate subset. The repulsion is provably and numerically bounded below by 0. Anti-collapse holds — constant prediction 6.62 vs 2.24 for the true prediction, and all three objectives are monotone increasing in isotropic error. The decisive check: on a synthetic batch shaped like the described data (an identical mv block plus boards of near-identical contents differing only on a canary coordinate subset), I compared the loss at the true prediction against the loss at a prediction with two board members' contents swapped. The new objective penalises the swap by +0.598 / +3.339 / +4.952 for 24 / 96 / 256 canary coordinates. Both parents PREFER the wrong prediction in the hardest case: r12 gives -0.144 and r22 gives -0.279 at 24 coordinates. That is precisely the pathology the hypothesis claims the inverse-error precision weight causes, demonstrated rather than argued — because at a good prediction mse_d is near zero everywhere and the parents' weight is uniform, while at a content-wrong prediction mse_d spikes on exactly the canary coordinates and the parents down-weight them. I also verified the hypothesis's criticism of the parent's absolute-margin hinge: at a perfect prediction r12's repulsion is softplus(1.76)=1.92 for near pairs, unsatisfiable, whereas the new normalised hinge is at softplus(-2.5)=0.079. Cost, which the author honestly flagged as unmeasured: the loss alone is 0.138s vs the parent's 0.060s (2.3x) for forward+backward at n=1920, d=768 on CPU, but inside a full training step with the r18 arch and r2 head the candidate ran 12.17s vs 13.60s for 12 steps — no net slowdown. Divergences are all documentation-level, listed above; none changes what the mechanism is. The one thing a reader of the archive should be told is that this is a two-axis change: stream also moves from baseline_interleave to r4_role_bound_path_atom_codes, so a score cannot attribute the effect to the objective. The author states this plainly as risk #4.

divergences.claim: "the r4 stream writes ... a role-bound sign code that is literally (role_src * hash(src_path) + hash(src_path)) + (role_dst * hash(dst_path) + hash(dst_path))"
divergences.what_the_code_does: evolve/chunks/stream/r4_role_bound_path_atom_codes.py:_build_code also seeds the vector with a verb/redirect SHAPE atom (SHAPE_ROLE=0.40) and adds a basename atom pair per path (BASE_ROLE=0.22 role-bound, BASE_FREE=0.30 free), and scales the full-path terms by FULL_ROLE=0.75 / FULL_FREE=0.55. The word "literally" describes a strict subset of the code. This is inherited code, not the candidate's own invention, and the structural properties the hypothesis relies on (per-command-string, position-local, prefix-causal, last 128 of 768 coords, observations untouched) are all true.
divergences.evidence: evolve/chunks/stream/r4_role_bound_path_atom_codes.py lines for _build_code / _slots; CODE_OFF = D - 128 = 640, out[:, 640:] = code in code_cmds.

divergences.claim: "every scale in the loss (equivalence threshold, ring width, duplicate suppression, softmax temperature, gap floor) is now a fraction of the class-measured mean off-diagonal target distance"
divergences.what_the_code_does: The equivalence threshold is a fraction of `mean_all`, the PLAIN unweighted off-diagonal mean computed before classes exist (line 61-62: mean_all = (tt*(~eye)).sum()/(n(n-1)); equivalent = tt <= _EQ_FRAC*mean_all). Only ring width, duplicate suppression, temperature and gap floor use the class-measured `mean_off`/`mean_offw`. Unavoidable ordering, and numerically irrelevant at _EQ_FRAC=1e-3, but the sentence is inaccurate as written.

divergences.claim: The hypothesis presents the repulsion as a redesigned form of the parents' hinge and never mentions a weight change.
divergences.what_the_code_does: _LAMBDA_REP = 0.25, against 0.1 in BOTH parents (r12 and r22). A silent 2.5x reweighting of the repulsion term. Measured effect at a realistic operating point is small — the term contributes ~0.020 of a ~2.26 total loss and varies only from 0.0197 (perfect prediction) to 0.0204 (noise 0.9), because the new gap-normalised hinge is essentially satisfied at truth (slack=1 >= 0.5, softplus(-2.5)=0.079) — but it is an undisclosed hyperparameter change.
divergences.evidence: impl line 38 `_LAMBDA_REP = 0.25`; BRIEF parent r12 `_LAMBDA_REP = 0.1`; partner r22 `_LAMBDA_REP = 0.1`. Decomposed loss run: listwise 2.2129 / anchor 0.0406 / 0.25*repulsion 0.0204 at noise 0.9 vs 2.2192 / 0.0 / 0.0197 at perfect.

divergences.claim: "v_d = sum_{i,j} r_ij * (t_id - t_jd)^2 / ||t_i - t_j||^2 ... Because sum_d (t_id-t_jd)^2/||t_i-t_j||^2 = 1 exactly, v is a probability-like distribution of the decision directions over coordinates"
divergences.what_the_code_does: The code divides by gap_eff = max(||t_i-t_j||^2, 0.1*d*mean_off), not by ||t_i-t_j||^2 (lines 83-86). For pairs closer than 10% of the mean gap the per-pair contribution sums to g_true/g_floor < 1, so the CLOSEST — i.e. the most decision-relevant — pairs are down-weighted in the metric, the opposite direction from the hypothesis's own rationale. The hypothesis names the gap floor only in connection with the hinge and never notes that the same floored quantity enters v_d. In a synthetic batch shaped like the described data the floor bound 0.8% of distinct pairs but ~10% of total ring mass, so the effect is real but second-order.
divergences.evidence: impl lines 83-86 (`gap_floor`, `gap_eff`, `rn = ringw / gap_eff`) vs hypothesis line 54. Measured: frac pairs floored 0.0076, ring mass floored 0.102 on a 620-row synthetic batch with a 300-row identical-observation block.
